title: Snowflake Bentley
hook: A Vermont farmer who spent his life photographing single snowflakes.
peek: Wilson Bentley, a farmer from Jericho, Vermont, took the first known photograph of a single snowflake in 1885. Over the next 46 years he captured thousands more, and his pictures shaped the idea that no two are alike.
lede: Wilson Bentley grew up on a farm in Jericho, Vermont, and fell in love with snow crystals under a small microscope his mother gave him. On 15 January 1885, aged 19, he rigged a bellows camera to a microscope and took the first known photograph of a single snowflake. He kept going for 46 winters and photographed more than 5,000.

bullets.text: Bentley caught flakes on a black board, lifted them with a thin splint or feather and worked in an unheated shed so nothing melted. Each image had to be made in moments.
Bentley's pictures helped popularise the idea that no two snowflakes are the same. In his photographs each crystal looked different, shaped by its own path through changing temperature and humidity.
Bentley also studied rain. He let drops fall into pans of flour, which set into little pellets he could measure, and he kept size records for hundreds of storms, early work on how raindrops form.
In 1931, he and the physicist W. J. Humphreys published a book of more than 2,000 of his photographs. It is still in print and still used by artists and designers.
